title: Cohomology of the projective line and the trace
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an integer $r\geq1$, and a finite commutative $\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$-algebra $\Lambda$. On each site the coefficient ring sheaf is the constant sheaf associated to the finite discrete ring $\Lambda$; the Tate twists below need only be locally constant. Use the small pro-etale site and its ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor], and the exact inverse image and derived direct image with their adjunction [sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors]. For a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, put $\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1)=\mu_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}\Lambda_T$, and $\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(-1)=\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1),\Lambda_T)$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-sheaf]. Define $\Lambda_T(\pm1)=\nu_T^*\Lambda_{T,\mathrm{et}}(\pm1)$ using the etale/pro-etale comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and $K(1)=K\otimes_\Lambda^L\Lambda_T(1)$. The Chern class is the scalar-extended Kummer boundary, pulled through $\nu_T^*$; it is also the Cartier class composite of [sk-lem-geo-cartier]. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. The line bundle $\mathcal O(1)$ is given on the standard charts by the degree-one transition $e_i=(x_i/x_j)e_j$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. A Noetherian scheme means one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings.

Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible and
$p:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ the projection. The unit
$\Lambda_S\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}$ and the class
$c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1))$ define an isomorphism

$$
\Lambda_S\oplus\Lambda_S(-1)[-2]
      \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}
      \quad\text{in }D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda),   \qquad\text{(G2)}
$$

compatible with base change: for $g:S'\to S$ with $S'$ as in the lemma, the
base-change map $g^*Rp_*\Lambda\to Rp'_*\Lambda$ in
$D(S'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ carries the pullback of (G2) to (G2) for $S'$.
Let

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_p:Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]\longrightarrow\Lambda_S
\qquad\text{(G3)}
$$

be the morphism in $D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ given by the projection onto
the summand $\Lambda_S$ of the twist of (G2). Then $\operatorname{Tr}_p$ is
compatible with every Noetherian base change.

proof.text: Use the ordinary étale projective-line decomposition and normalized trace datum. Chern-class injectivity identifies the specified Chern arrows. Uniqueness of normalized finite Tate transport identifies the shifted positive-line comparison with the signed-twist pullback.

The exact comparison preserves binary biproducts. The counit mate for direct image is invertible on the degree-zero constant object and on the positive Tate line shifted by two, since both are bounded below and projective-line projection is qcqs. Apply it to the étale untwisted and twisted decompositions.

Restrict the fixed D+ exchange comparison to the unbounded category, using compatibility of the exact étale exchange with D+ inclusion. Conjugate by the exact-versus-left-derived inverse-image isomorphisms. Naturality of the pullback comparison and the direct-image counit mate transfers both étale decomposition squares. The binary biproduct universal property identifies the source maps.

Choose each twisted isomorphism by asIso of its specified map, whose invertibility was proved. Invert its commuting base-change square and project onto the constant second summand. The biproduct projection identity gives exactly the stated trace equation.

Step 1: the chart calculation gives D=V(x0) and O(D) with e0=(x0/x1)e1, the same as def-pc-projective-space-twist and the convention of the Kummer-class definition, and D stays Cartier after every base change. Step 2: I wrote out the mate calculation for the class component myself; it takes two lines. Step 3: the fibre-cohomology corollary applies (finite ring, D^+), the genus is 0 so H^1=0, the degree-coordinate lemma applies with k=K and empty boundary, and degree one comes from the rational-point lemma. Step 4: the hypotheses of lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection hold, U(beta)=PF is an isomorphism by lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection, and its adjunct is L_Z(x^flat), so the components are exactly the scalar unit and the scalar Kummer class; flatness of Lambda is never used. Steps 5-8: the projection formula, evaluation, exchange/tensor coherence, the comparison C_p (p qcqs, D^+) and the formal mate lemma are each used for exactly what their statements say. Step 8 also proves that the pro-etale projection map is an isomorphism, which (G3) needs. Step 9 is genuinely elementary. The coefficient category and base-change map are the classical pro-etale ones of sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison and sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors. The route matches the unit, and thm-amb-p1-decomposition is already recorded as same_as with no new duplicate. I accept the new tool uses lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection, lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates and lem-sc-primitive-root (Lean closed). The return points (hidden lemmas in old steps 2 and 5, step length) are repaired. No changes.

lean.note: The constants and finite signed twists are exact comparison pullbacks of the ordinary etale module objects. Both decomposition maps use the same existing Kummer-normalized Chern arrow; the direct-image comparison and geometric exchange are their canonical counit mates. The trace is the inverse twisted decomposition followed by the constant-summand projection. No new coefficient category or arbitrary comparison is chosen.
